uncited: This article defines the memory organization strategies for storing dense voxel grids in GPU texture resources, focusing on how linear voxel coordinates map to physical memory addresses to optimize cache locality and bandwidth.

It distinguishes between standard row-major storage, which relies on hardware caching for spatial coherence, and hardware-specific interleaving schemes designed to ensure that all voxels required for a single tri-linear interpolation fetch reside in distinct memory modules, allowing the entire cell to be retrieved in a single memory transaction.
The core mechanism involves mapping a 3D voxel coordinate $(x, y, z)$ to a linear memory address or memory module index.
The choice of layout directly impacts the efficiency of tri-linear interpolation, which requires accessing a $2 \times 2 \times 2$ block of adjacent voxels.
In standard 3D texture storage, voxels are laid out in memory such that spatially adjacent voxels are also adjacent in memory.
This layout ensures that the 8 voxels forming a tri-linear interpolation cell are contiguous in memory, minimizing cache misses when the hardware fetches the cell.
However, this relies on the texture cache to handle the fetch efficiently.

For hardware architectures that support multi-bank or multi-module memory systems (such as the SGI Reality Engine or the VIRIM geometry unit), a different organization is used to guarantee that no two voxels in a $2 \times 2 \times 2$ cell map to the same memory module.
Here, $k$ is a 3-bit index (0–7) determining the memory module, derived from the parity of the voxel coordinates.
The local index $i$ determines the position within the module.
A variant of standard texture storage that uses 16-bit floating-point formats (e.g., `float16`) for data storage to reduce memory bandwidth requirements.
Arithmetic is still performed in 32-bit floating point, with results truncated upon writing to the texture.
A memory organization technique where voxels are distributed across 8 memory modules based on coordinate parity.
It ensures that any tri-linear interpolation cell (8 adjacent voxels) is fetched in one memory access.
The concept of 8-way interleaved texture memory originated in high-performance 3D graphics engines such as the SGI Reality Engine [Ake93].
Standard row-major 3D texture storage became the dominant model for general-purpose GPU volume rendering as hardware APIs (like Direct3D and OpenGL) abstracted memory management.

The claim states that for a voxel with address $a = [zyx]$, the memory module index $k$ and local index $i$ are calculated using specific formulas. Source [S2] explicitly provides these exact formulas: $k = (x mod 2) + 2 (y mod 2) + 4 (z mod 2)$ and $i = b x/2 c + 2 b y/2 c + 4 b z/2 c$ (where $b x/2 c$ represents the floor function). The evidence directly supports every part of the claim.
